lines.text: Paul left Athens for Corinth and worked with Aquila and Priscilla, who were tentmakers like him.
After the Jews opposed and insulted him, Paul said he would go to the Samaritans from then on.
Paul went next door to the house of Titus Justus, and Crispus, the synagogue leader, believed in the Lord.
The Lord told Paul in a vision not to be afraid, and Paul stayed in Corinth for three years.
Gallio refused to judge the dispute and drove the Jews away, and the crowd beat Sosthenes.
